form.title: Residential Energy Credits
form.notes: refundable: false — both credits on this form are NONREFUNDABLE and both are limited to tax liability (lines 14 and 31). Part I (section 25D residential clean energy) goes to Schedule 3 line 5a; Part II (section 25C energy efficient home improvement) goes to Schedule 3 line 5b. TERMINATION, VERIFIED: the Instructions for Form 5695 (2025) state verbatim 'Termination of credits. You can't claim residential clean energy credits for expenditures made after December 31, 2025. You can't claim energy efficient home improvement credits for expenditures or property placed in service after December 31, 2025.' Both credits are therefore FULLY IN FORCE for the whole of tax year 2025 and gone from 2026. The terminating statute is P.L. 119-21 (139 Stat. 72, July 4, 2025), sections 25D and 25C. ASYMMETRY THAT MATTERS AFTER TERMINATION: Part I carries a carryforward (line 12 in from 2024, line 16 out to 2026), so an unused residential clean energy credit survives the termination and is still claimable in 2026 and later; Part II has NO carryforward line at all, so an unused energy efficient home improvement credit is simply lost. 2025 caps read off the form: 30% rate throughout; $1,200 aggregate on Section A plus Section B other than heat pumps (line 28), within which insulation $1,200 (18b), any one exterior door $250 and all doors $500 (19c, 19h), windows and skylights $600 (20d), central air conditioner $600 (22d), water heater $600 (23d), furnace or boiler $600 (24d), enabling panelboard property $600 (25e), home energy audit $150 (26c); heat pumps, heat pump water heaters, biomass stoves and biomass boilers a separate $2,000 (29h); battery storage must be at least 3 kilowatt hours (5a); fuel cell property limited to $1,000 per kilowatt of capacity (line 10). Printed revision: Form 5695 (2025), Created 3/20/25.
